summary: Construct structured dense-parity rows with a global odd-mass dual obstruction near the half-degree cutoff.
Determine static barriers or ceilings for logarithmic-width affine rows, comparing NS/PC separations with low-degree testing on flats.
Analyze product-tree standard monomials and find a contradiction whose proper closure survives into the small-extension-count regime.
Compare small extension counts with existence of an odd-mass static dual function on one explicit family.
Test higher-arity trees and sum definitions for a better cutoff-to-ceiling ratio than the product-tree frame.
Construct an unsatisfiable system with proper degree-D closure but shattered dimension far below its free dimension.
Determine whether near-2K shattered dimension or declining down-set levels are necessary for the engine, not just its dimension proof.
Bound truncated shattering from row-join structure and evaluate it on paired-source and dense-parity systems.
Bound extension counts uniformly over all scope-free sets in threshold-density random 3-CNF and compare the thin threshold.
Find formulas with dense low-width consequences but no degree-D refutation, such as hidden contradictions in dense implication structures.
Seek a non-monomial or rank-asymmetric pseudo-reduction for independent linear-form rows and audit the Alekhnovich–Razborov transfer.
Bound F2 PC degree for three-occurrence CNFs via elimination or incidence width and compare the candidate lower-bound constants.
Translate cubic-incidence pathwidth or cutwidth bounds into a PC-degree ceiling below half the variable count.
Determine whether two-rail CNF encoding doubles F2 PC degree or only the variable count, preserving the absence of exclusivity axioms.
Consolidate route decisions and require review tests assigned to the nearest queue item to say when their questions differ.
Extend the method ceiling to nonminimal formulas by respectful-neighbor pruning and evaluate graph pigeonhole formulas.
Read code-product distance and uniformity theorems to test whether binary code triples meet the low-degree product-row hypotheses.
Decide whether binary code pairs have both linear dual distances and linear product distance, distinguishing plain from stabilizer-relative distance.
Prove existence or an obstruction for binary codes with simultaneous linear dual and square distance, also allowing unequal pairs.
Derive rank versions of the support definitions and random-form deficiency bound only after a viable pseudo-reduction is found.
Prove a sub-half linear upper bound or a lower bound for random products of two affine forms at constant density.
Prove absence of nonforced low-degree falls for random parity clauses at covering density, starting with degree three and width two.
Read explicit F2 analytic-rank versus partition-rank bounds and determine their useful range for the random cubic-functional bias tail.
Test and resolve the random-plane hypothesis beyond its base range using exact intersections where failure is possible.
Prove the quadratic colon identity uniformly over nonzero vectors and count projected rank-two span elements.
Construct certificates as sums of decomposable trivectors, or lower-bound the number of terms needed at higher row density.
Derive sharp point probabilities for sums of independent decomposable trivectors through fixed vectors.
Classify projected degree-three relations for vectors supported on several general-position planes and count the surviving random-plane witnesses.
Read exact regularity results for random Boolean quadratics and check whether products of affine forms satisfy their hypotheses.
Use explicit F2 analytic-rank bounds to count low-partition-rank symmetric trilinear forms at the needed density.
Verify the two convexity steps in the slice-rank first-moment bound and count alternating tensors by their slice-rank profiles.
Determine whether degree three at intermediate quadratic row density falls within the cumulative-index-span conjecture.
Scale parity two-clause degree calculations using structured elimination or a degree-capped Gröbner engine, sized from measured runs.
Repeat the static test with all multipliers to determine whether excess over the series index comes from the counting convention.
Derive the generating series' regularity-index asymptotics at the stated density without claiming a theorem about underlying systems.
Use lcm-lattice homology to locate cancellations, then lift actual tails and subsequent relations with explicit PC costs.
Determine the least refutation degree of three pairwise-consistent but jointly-unsatisfiable rows from widths and overlaps.
Compute the dependency-series factors when projected planes have rank one or zero, the typical finite-field degeneracies.
Extend colon recursion and the series lower-bound lemma to width k, with a full-range width-three control.
Construct structured width-two plane families with a closed-form quotient attaining the predicted series below its index.
